userStories.title: Make room in the chat host without changing behavior
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extract session listing and final resource close so the host has space for ACP glue.

**Motivation** — The user wants to use the subscriptions already paid for (Claude, Codex, Cursor) and each agent's own skills from inside the nax chat TUI, while keeping nax's plan / run / bot tools and the job list (design §1, G1–G5).

**Approach** — Two pure moves out of `chat-host.ts`: `allSessions` / `latestId` become `listCwdSessions(storage, cwd)` and `latestResumableId({ storage, cwd, logger })` in new `src/chat/session-listing.ts`, and `closeSessionAndResources` becomes `closeChatResources({ hygiene, handle, tasks, resources, chain })` in `src/chat/session-hygiene.ts`. The host calls them; behaviour is unchanged and `chat-host.ts` ends at most 560 lines.

`packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts` is at the 600-line limit and must stay at or under it (`check:file-sizes`). US-002 first makes room with two pure moves: the session listing (`allSessions` / `latestId`) into new `session-listing.ts`, and the final resource close (`closeSessionAndResources`) into `session-hygiene.ts` as `closeChatResources`, bringing the file to at most 560 lines. `primeContextWindow` and `_chatHostDeps` stay in the host (`chat-host-context-window.test.ts` stubs that seam).

Preserve pagination in page order, cwd/cursor arguments, metadata identity and mode validation, live-lock exclusion, unreadable-metadata warning/rethrow distinctions and nested finally cleanup ordering/error precedence.

**Scope** — In: pure extraction plus host call-site replacement and behavioral regressions. Out: catalog getters (US-008), ACP opener/refusal wiring (US-009/010), changing session eligibility or cleanup semantics.

**Interface** — `listCwdSessions(storage, cwd)`; `latestResumableId({ storage, cwd, logger })`; `closeChatResources({ hygiene, handle, tasks, resources, chain })`.

userStories.title: Deliver workflow tools and mode-neutral ACP instructions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Adapt only chat workflow/jobs providers into ACP embedder tools and add a separate mode-neutral prompt builder.

**Motivation** — The user wants to use the subscriptions already paid for (Claude, Codex, Cursor) and each agent's own skills from inside the nax chat TUI, while keeping nax's plan / run / bot tools and the job list (design §1, G1–G5).

**Approach** — Of the chat's tool providers, only `nax-workflow` and `nax-jobs` are delivered, resolved with nax-agent's `resolveProviderTools` and turned into embedder tools with nax's existing `toEmbedderTools` (`approval: "never"`: the jobs tools already ask the person themselves through `ChatAskController.requestHostApproval`). Their instructions are rendered with `renderProviderInstructions` into the ACP brain's system instructions.

The ACP brain's system instructions are mode-neutral: an ACP session receives them once (a reopen by resume does not resend them, `instructionsSent` in nax-agent-acp's `backend.ts`), so a mode toggle must not leave them stating the wrong mode.

Use stage `"chat"` for provider resolution; a provider whose `tools()` rejects is dropped. Omit `instructions` when absent. Leave buildChatInstructions and its output unchanged. `toEmbedderTools` already uses `approval: "never"`; a throw becomes an `isError` result. Verification note: `bun run check:import-cycles` stays green with `@/chat` importing `@/agents/acp`.

**Scope** — In: acp-tools.ts, toEmbedderTools re-export from agents/acp, buildChatAcpInstructions and prompts barrel export. Out: building/opening sessions (US-005/006), attaching catalog/host glue (US-007–010). Bridging nax's background Bash and ctrl+b, nax subagents, the nax skill loader, nax's MCP pool, nax compaction, the command shadow or nax's rules delivery to an ACP brain; they step aside (the agent's own equivalents apply). Workflow tools on the `nax-agent` ACP server that koda connects to; a separate later feature. Resending the ACP brain's system instructions on a reopen; they are mode-neutral, so nothing in them goes stale.

**Interface**
```ts
export const ACP_CHAT_PROVIDER_IDS: readonly string[]; // ["nax-workflow", "nax-jobs"]
export interface ChatAcpTools { readonly tools: readonly EmbedderTool[]; readonly instructions?: string }
export function chatAcpTools(providers: readonly ToolProvider[], workdir: string): Promise<ChatAcpTools>;

export function buildChatAcpInstructions(input: { agentLabel: string; toolInstructions?: string }): string;
```
Existing adapter to re-export: `toEmbedderTools(tools: readonly CodingTool[], workdir: string): EmbedderTool[]`.

userStories.title: Open chat on an ACP brain with per-agent transcripts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Select ACP session creation/resume from metadata without changing native chat behavior.

**Motivation** — A stored session document refuses to reopen on another backend (`checkBackendKind` in `packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-resume.ts`, `AGENT_SESSION_BACKEND_MISMATCH`), and the chat keeps one session id across model switches. So each brain keeps its own transcript document: the native one where it is today, each agent's under `<sessions dir>/acp-<agent>/`. Carrying the conversation from one brain to the next is F3.

**Approach** — `openChatSession` reads the session's model. For an ACP model it opens `acpBackend` with a file transcript store in `<sessions dir>/acp-<agent>/` (same session id), creating the agent session when that store has no document and resuming it otherwise. The handle's `history` is always the native document's messages, so `/resume` keeps replaying what the native brain said.

For an ACP model (US-006) the options come from `acpSessionOptions`, the agent store is `createFileTranscriptStore(acpTranscriptDir(storage.dir, agent))`, no command shadow is built, and `history` is read from the native store. `parseChatAcpModel(meta.model)` runs before the storage lock is acquired, so an invalid model string never holds the lock. A resume of the agent document that fails with an error `isFreshFallback` accepts (code `AGENT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `AGENT_SESSION_BACKEND_MISMATCH` or `TRANSCRIPT_CORRUPT`, or `AGENT_SESSION_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED` whose `context.capability` is `"resume"`: the stored agent session is unusable) retains the document (`retainFailed`), creates a fresh agent session, and returns a handle whose new optional `notice` is `ACP_FRESH_SESSION_NOTICE(label)`; any other failure propagates. `ChatSessionHandle` gains `readonly notice?: string`.

Resuming it fails with any other error (`AGENT_SESSION_AUTH_REQUIRED`, `AGENT_SESSION_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`, a timeout, or `AGENT_SESSION_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED` for `"model"` when the restored session offers no model option): the error propagates and the document is kept; a switch rolls back to the previous brain (`switchSession`). Any other ACP open failure (`AGENT_SESSION_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED` on a new session, `AGENT_SESSION_MODEL_MISMATCH`, a timeout) propagates; the catalog records nothing (US-007/009). Keep the native branch of openChatSession as it is (its options, its single native transcript store call and its history), and the ACP seams live on the new _acpSessionDeps. Preserve release/lock cleanup on every error.

**Scope** — In: ACP branch, separate agent store, native history, invalid-before-lock validation, retained-and-fresh fallback and optional notice. Out: host reporting/rollback changes (US-009). Carrying the conversation across a brain switch, recording ACP turns in nax's transcript, and replaying earlier turns into a newly opened agent; feature F3. Until then each brain sees only its own turns. Showing an ACP brain's own earlier turns when a session is resumed; `history` replays the native document only (F3). Removing an empty session's ACP transcript document or the agent's own session when the empty chat session's metadata is removed. Changing an agent's model when its restored session offers no model option: nax-agent-acp refuses (`capability: "model"`), the error propagates and the switch rolls back; nax does not start a fresh agent session for it.

**Interface** — `ChatSessionHandle` gains `readonly notice?: string`; retain `openChatSession(request: OpenChatSessionRequest, deps = _openChatSessionDeps): Promise<ChatSessionHandle>` and use US-005's `acpSessionOptions`, `acpTranscriptDir`, `isFreshFallback` and `ACP_FRESH_SESSION_NOTICE`.

[integration] When resuming an ACP document fails with AGENT_SESSION_BACKEND_MISMATCH or TRANSCRIPT_CORRUPT, openChatSession retains the failed agent document before creating a fresh session with the same session id; and When resuming an ACP document fails with AGENT_SESSION_BACKEND_MISMATCH or TRANSCRIPT_CORRUPT, the returned handle.notice equals ACP_FRESH_SESSION_NOTICE for that agent label.
[integration] When resuming an ACP document fails with a timeout, openChatSession rejects with that error without replacing the stored document.

[integration] When a new ACP session open fails with AGENT_SESSION_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED, AGENT_SESSION_MODEL_MISMATCH or a timeout, openChatSession propagates that error without taking a fresh-session fallback.
[integration] When a nax-workflow or nax-jobs provider's tools() rejects, openChatSession still opens the ACP session with no tools from that provider.

routing.reasoning: Integrates backend dispatch, locks, dual transcript stores and narrowly permitted resume recovery; security-sensitive session persistence requires strict isolation.

userStories.title: Expose ACP choices through the host and chat CLI
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Compose the ACP catalog into chat and expose live models, efforts and availability notes.

**Motivation** — Rulings 2026-10-29: an ACP agent is a main model choice in the chat picker; Claude Code, Codex and Cursor ship together; each loads its own full setup (its own allow rules and hooks act without a nax card); koda's ACP-server side is a separate feature.

**Approach** — `ChatHostDeps.acp?: AcpCatalog`; `models` is a getter returning the deps' models followed by `acp.rows()`; `effortLevels(model)` for an ACP model returns `acp.effortLevels(model)` (`["default"]` without a catalog); new `modelNote(model)` returns `acp?.unavailable(model)`. Preserve tierModels fallback for native models when deps.models is absent. `ChatHostDeps.acp` and `ChatHost.modelNote` are optional, and a host without a catalog keeps today's models list, so the existing CLI and host model assertions hold.

`packages/nax/src/cli/chat.ts` — `_chatCommandDeps.createAcpCatalog` (production `createAcpCatalog`); `composeChat` passes `acp: deps.createAcpCatalog({ env: deps.env })` to `createChatHost`. The host exposes it through `models`, `effortLevels` and a new optional `modelNote`.

US-007 → US-008: `createAcpCatalog` is built by `chatCommand` (US-008 AC stubs `_chatCommandDeps.createAcpCatalog` and observes `createChatHost`'s input).

**Scope** — In: host optional catalog field, dynamic getters and effort/note methods, injected CLI catalog factory. Out: open reporting/availability refusal/context/commands (US-009), guarded write hook (US-010), labels (US-011) and slash step-aside (US-012). Keep the room made by US-002; glue belongs outside the host.

**Interface** — `ChatHostDeps` gains `readonly acp?: AcpCatalog`; `ChatHost` gains the optional `modelNote?(model: string): string | undefined`. Existing host `models` remains `readonly string[]` at its interface, backed by a getter. `effortLevels(model)` delegates only ACP models to the catalog and otherwise preserves the deps map or EFFORT_LEVELS.

userStories.title: Open, refuse and report ACP brains through the host
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Connect host lifecycle to ACP availability and open reporting while preserving rollback and session identity.

**Motivation** — Rulings 2026-10-30 (this spec): the picker shows the models (and effort levels) an agent offers after its first open; an agent whose binary is missing is shown as unavailable with the reason; while a chat-started `nax plan` / `nax run` job holds the checkout, guarded mode rejects the agent's file-edit permission requests (full mode cannot be guarded, because the agent never asks).

**Approach** — Every open goes through `reportAcpOpens` (reports `acp.opened` / `acp.failed` for ACP models); start and switch to an ACP model whose agent is not installed throw `CHAT_ACP_AGENT_UNAVAILABLE` (via `assertAcpInstalled`) before the current session is closed; `primeContextWindow` never looks up an ACP model; `runCommand` on an ACP model returns `ACP_RUN_COMMAND_UNSUPPORTED`; `notice()` returns the resume notice, else the current handle's `notice`. The file stays at or under 600 lines.

US-008, US-009 and US-010 then put the ACP glue in `src/chat/acp/acp-host.ts` and `acp-write-guard.ts`, leaving one-line call sites in the host: the host wraps its opener once (`this.open = reportAcpOpens(...)`, replacing the three `this.deps.open ?? openChatSession` sites), calls `assertAcpInstalled` before opening or closing anything, and passes `acpRefusal(...)` as the ask controller's `refuse` (US-010). `primeContextWindow` and `_chatHostDeps` stay in the host (`chat-host-context-window.test.ts` stubs that seam).

Start or switch to an ACP model whose agent's binary does not resolve: `CHAT_ACP_AGENT_UNAVAILABLE` (`stage: "chat"`, message names the agent label and `not installed`); the current session stays open and unchanged. An ACP open fails with `AGENT_SESSION_AUTH_REQUIRED`: the catalog records `not logged in`; the error propagates as today (a switch reopens the previous brain, `switchSession`'s rollback). Other failures propagate through the existing rollback. `reportAcpOpens` forwards every open's arguments unchanged, so existing assertions on the open stub's calls hold.

US-001 → US-007 → US-009: the capability report's `offeredModels` / `offeredEfforts` reach the catalog through the host's open reporting (US-009 ACs open a stubbed ACP session whose `backend.capabilities` carries them and read `host.models`).

**Scope** — In: acp-host helpers and thin host lifecycle call sites, availability preflight, context skip, run-command refusal and notice precedence. Out: session-store/fresh-fallback implementation (US-006), catalog state policy (US-007), ask refusal (US-010), pid registry integration or history carry.

**Interface**
```ts
/**
 * Wraps an opener, forwarding (request, deps) unchanged. On success it reports
 * catalog.opened(handle.meta.model, handle.session.backend.capabilities) when that model is an
 * ACP model; on failure it reports catalog.failed(request.model, error) when request.model is an
 * ACP model (a resume request carries no model, so its failure is not recorded), then rethrows.
 */
export function reportAcpOpens(open: typeof openChatSession, catalog: AcpCatalog | undefined): typeof openChatSession;
/** Throws CHAT_ACP_AGENT_UNAVAILABLE for an ACP model whose agent is not installed; no-op otherwise or without a catalog. */
export function assertAcpInstalled(catalog: AcpCatalog | undefined, model: string): void;
```

userStories.title: Name ACP brains in the picker, status and switch notices
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Render human-readable ACP names and availability details, and warn when switching to a brain that cannot see prior turns.

**Motivation** — The user wants to use the subscriptions already paid for (Claude, Codex, Cursor) and each agent's own skills from inside the nax chat TUI, while keeping nax's plan / run / bot tools and the job list (design §1, G1–G5).

**Approach** — `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/chat-status.ts` — `modelParts(raw)` names an ACP model by `acpModelLabel` (name = the label without its effort suffix, suffix = `[<effort>]`), so `shortModel` and the header use it.

`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/picker-model.ts` — `PickerModelInput` gains `modelNote?: (model: string) => string | undefined`; an ACP row's label is `acpModelLabel(base)`; a row with a note shows `unavailable: <note>` as its detail. `useChatPicker` passes `modelNote: (model) => host.modelNote?.(model)` (a bound call, never the bare method).

`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/use-switch-notices.ts` — the model notice names a model as `shortModel` does (an ACP model by `acpModelLabel`, a native one by its name after the last `/`, effort suffix kept); a brain change (native to ACP, ACP to native, or one agent to another) adds a second notice `<new name> does not see <old name>'s turns`.

US-008 → US-011: `host.modelNote` reaches the picker through `useChatPicker` (US-011 AC renders the picker through the hook for a host built by `createChatHost`). Preserve existing native labels, details, notices and filtering; malformed acp metadata labels must not throw at render time. Same-agent model/effort changes are not brain changes; existing same-session comparison suppresses mount/resume notices.

**Scope** — In: modelParts/shortModel/header labels, picker note callback and labels, bound hook forwarding, brain-change notices. Out: catalog/host models policy (US-007/008), slash menu/commands (US-012), conversation transfer or ACP history replay.

**Interface** — `PickerModelInput` gains `modelNote?: (model: string) => string | undefined`; consume `ChatHost.modelNote?(model: string): string | undefined` with a closure. Preserve `shortModel(model: string): string` and `useSwitchNotices(state: ChatHostState, append: (entry: TranscriptEntry) => void): void`.

userStories.title: Make native-only slash features step aside on ACP
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Keep built-in chat controls while handing non-built-in slash text to the ACP agent's own command system.

**Motivation** — Rulings 2026-10-29: an ACP agent is a main model choice in the chat picker; Claude Code, Codex and Cursor ship together; each loads its own full setup (its own allow rules and hooks act without a nax card); koda's ACP-server side is a separate feature.

**Approach** — On an ACP brain `/skills`, `/mcp` and `/agents` say they are not available, any slash command that is not a built-in is sent to the agent as typed (agents have their own commands), `/help` and the slash menu list built-ins only, and `!` commands say they run on native models only (US-009 owns the ! refusal).

`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/slash-commands.ts`, `packages/nax/src/tui/chat/slash-menu.ts` — the ACP step-aside (US-012). `SlashMenuHost` becomes `Pick<ChatHost, "catalog"> & Partial<Pick<ChatHost, "current">>`; when `current` is absent or throws (no session open yet), the menu offers built-ins plus the catalog, as today.

`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx` — the memo also depends on the session's current model, so the menu changes when the brain switches between native and ACP. The baseline `const menuItems = useMemo(() => slashMenuItems(host), [host]);` is replaced with a memo that follows current model as well as host.

`/skills`, `/mcp`, `/agents`, unknown slash commands, `/help` and the slash menu on an ACP brain, and `ChatApp`'s menu memo following the current model. Every other built-in (`/plugins`, `/feature`, `/jobs`, `/cost`, `/sessions`, `/resume`, `/clear`, `/mode`, `/model`, `/effort`, `/quit`) behaves on an ACP brain as it does today. US-008 → US-012: the host's current model reaches the slash menu through `ChatApp` (US-012 AC renders `ChatApp` and switches the model). Preserve native labels, details, notices, commands and menu.

**Scope** — In: ACP slash notices/dispatch/help/menu, optional-current fallback and model-dependent ChatApp memo. Out: catalog/host lifecycle (US-007–009), ! command implementation (US-009), picker/status labels (US-011), loading nax skills/MCP/subagents into ACP or ACP history carry.

**Interface**
```ts
export type SlashMenuHost = Pick<ChatHost, "catalog"> & Partial<Pick<ChatHost, "current">>;
```
Non-built-in ACP outcomes retain `SlashOutcome`'s `{ kind: "send"; message: string }`, preserving the slash invocation and arguments exactly as typed.

analysis:
Refine audit: manually mapped all 187 numbered spec acceptance criteria (US-001:16, US-002:15, US-003:21, US-004:15, US-005:13, US-006:17, US-007:17, US-008:10, US-009:17, US-010:16, US-011:15, US-012:15) to their original stories, retaining split assertions and regression qualifiers. All 21 feature exclusions remain verbatim; all 12 binding ids, workdirs, dependencies, expected outputs and spec context-file lists are unchanged. Negative cases exist in every story; explicit unavailable-note forwarding now anchors US-008's failure path, and native prompt output is anchored in US-004. No speculative helpers or package changes were introduced. Corrections: acpSessionOptions receives nested input.acp; resumeAgentSession receives (sessionId, options) with the store on options.transcriptStore; catalog learning is asserted through rows(), and ignored failures through unavailable(). ACP full-profile auto-decisions must stay allowed rather than be job-guarded, but do not assert transport event absence: packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/permissions.ts:140-171 records profile auto-decisions, and packages/nax/src/chat/ask-controller.ts:226 ignores answerable:false events before full-mode allowance. Preserve informational telemetry and refuse-before-full ordering for artificial answerable approvals. US-001 and US-010 are bounded medium patches with strict security TDD; US-011 is medium presentation logic with ordinary TDD. US-006/009 remain complex due to dual-store recovery and lifecycle rollback. This is a static manual audit, not an executed test or JSON-parser validation.

Feature F2 adds Claude Code, Codex and Cursor as selectable ACP brains to the existing native chat; F1's embedder-tool support is already present, and F3's cross-brain history is deliberately deferred. Exploration used direct reads and text searches because codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this host. No implementation changes or executable validation were performed while drafting this PRD.

Architecture and conventions: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:17 links the dependency-injection, errors and constants conventions; :151-152 documents the 600-line source hard limit and test-size rules. nax is Bun/React/Ink, while nax-agent-acp is a Node-compatible library: keep Bun APIs out of its source, use #src imports there, and consume nax-agent only through its public entry. nax consumes ACP only through @nathapp/nax-agent-acp/client. Keep prompts in the prompt builder, preserve barrel boundaries, use injectable _deps seams and fake ACP agents, and do not launch installed agents in CI. No package version bumps, nax-agent changes or nax-ai changes are required.

US-001/backend offers: packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/session-offers.ts:14 defines configOptions/modeIds/modelIds. capabilities.ts:104 flattens grouped select values, :119 sets MODEL_ID_MAX_CHARS=100, :129 resolves Cursor bare names, and :148 defines effort fallback ids (Cursor has none). text.ts:10 sets the minimum redacted secret length to 8; :62 cleanLabel removes controls/invisible characters, normalizes whitespace, scrubs secrets and caps code points. New offer extraction must accept an id only when cleaning returns it unchanged, deduplicate before capping to 50, preserve offer order and use the first thought_level option before the per-agent fallback. open.ts:63 defines OpenedAcp; :210 currently discards applyConfig's return; :280 applies mode, then model, then effort. applyMode/applyModel already return updated configOptions from set_config_option; return the post-model offers after applying effort, rather than the session/new snapshot or the effort answer. backend.ts:251 builds public BackendInfo from s.live.acp, and :269 exposes it through a getter, so reconnect must report the replacement process's offers. backend.ts:244 tracks instructionsSent across restores, and :319 sends instructions once. The fake script at test/fixtures/fake-agent/script.ts:105 has configOptions; agent.ts:327 validates configId and currently returns those original options. Add only the optional answer override, retaining that validation and default. Existing backend-codex.test.ts:74 opens the actual session facade with an in-memory agent and explicit fake command; test/helpers/in-memory-launch.ts:24 supplies launch/relaunch and process accounting. Mirror these fixtures for the new backend-offered-choices integration tests. Existing backend/open/capabilities/session-offers/reconnect tests provide regression coverage; additive capability fields must not disturb existing toMatchObject assertions.

US-002/host refactor: packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts is exactly 600 lines. allSessions at :358 paginates the cwd list; latestId at :370 filters metadata identity, non-empty/allowed mode and live locks, skipping only SESSION_META_UNREADABLE with a warning. Move them without semantic changes to session-listing.ts. closeSessionAndResources at :576 uses nested finally blocks to close the handle, stop tasks, tear down resources and destroy the chain even on error; move that unchanged control flow to closeChatResources in session-hygiene.ts. session-hygiene.ts:63 already owns close/release/empty-metadata removal. Preserve host teardown's operation draining (:562), close idempotence, lock-retention ordering and error precedence. Keep primeContextWindow and _chatHostDeps in the host; chat-host-context-window.test.ts:16 and :33 stub that exact seam. The refactor must bring the host to <=560 lines before glue is added; subsequent work must keep <=600. Existing chat-host.test.ts, chat-host-resume.test.ts and session-hygiene.test.ts cover public lifecycle behavior.

US-003/model namespace: packages/nax-agent/src/cost/model-spec.ts:31 accepts only one well-formed trailing effort suffix; malformed brackets are otherwise left as raw model text. Add chat-specific validation around that shared parser instead of changing native parsing. packages/nax/src/chat/chat-effort.ts:8 defines canonical order, :22 strips/adds suffixes, :29 filters supported efforts, and :64 clamps switch efforts. ACP strings are acp:<claude|codex|cursor>[/<model>][<effort>], with brackets forbidden in the remaining model id. Labels must never throw on malformed stored strings. Cursor offer reduction must deduplicate exact offered ids first, strip one trailing settings group, and omit ambiguous bare names; Claude/Codex bracketed offers cannot be selected and must be omitted. Do not cap again after reduction. Export the required public helpers through chat/acp/index.ts and chat/index.ts:1, preserving existing exports.

US-004/tools and prompts: packages/nax-agent/src/tools/provider-advertise.ts:113 resolves providers for a stage, namespaces/adapts tools and drops a provider whose tools() rejects (:139-164); instructions are optional and rendered separately. packages/nax/src/agents/acp/provider-embedder.ts:30 already converts CodingTool to EmbedderTool with approval never, root/workdir and signal forwarding, and converts thrown tool errors to isError results. Re-export it from agents/acp/index.ts, currently only three exports. Filter provider ids to nax-workflow/nax-jobs before resolveProviderTools(..., 'chat', workdir), and renderProviderInstructions only when present. The existing chat builder at prompts/builders/chat-builder.ts:24 embeds native mode/rules/sandbox content; leave buildChatInstructions byte-for-byte behavior unchanged and add a separate mode-neutral builder exported beside it in prompts/index.ts:52.
